title: Will wheat be more than 10% higher in 6 months?
why: Southern Italian durum yields fall in heat waves; a wheat spike hits pasta makers and bread prices.

title: Will wheat be more than 10% lower in 3 months?
why: A price slump squeezes French and Romanian growers already paying more for irrigation and inputs.

title: Will wheat be above $300/mt in 6 months?
why: $300/mt is roughly the stress line for EU food-import budgets and livestock feed.

title: Will maize be more than 10% higher in 6 months?
why: Summer droughts on the Danube plain cut Romanian maize, Europe's largest crop by area.

title: Will maize be above $250/mt in 3 months?
why: Spain imports feed maize for its pig sector; expensive feed hits rural livelihoods.

title: Will olive oil be more than 15% higher in 6 months?
why: Andalusian heat during flowering can halve the olive harvest and send prices up.

title: Will olive oil be above $7000/mt in 6 months?
why: Above $7000/mt olive oil becomes a crisis price for Greek and Italian households.

title: Will olive oil be more than 10% lower in 3 months?
why: A falling olive oil price signals a recovered Mediterranean harvest.

title: Will coffee be more than 10% higher in 6 months?
why: The EU imports all its coffee; Brazilian and Vietnamese droughts pass straight to European roasters.

title: Will coffee be above 300 USc/lb in 3 months?
why: 300 USc/lb is a historic extreme that strains Italian and German roasters.

title: Will cocoa be more than 15% higher in 6 months?
why: West African heat and disease drive cocoa; Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany are the main grinders.

title: Will cocoa be below $5000/mt in 6 months?
why: A return below $5000/mt would ease the European chocolate industry's input shock.

title: Will sugar be more than 10% higher in 6 months?
why: Dry summers and pest bans cut French beet yields while monsoon failures move world sugar.

title: Will sunflower oil be more than 10% higher in 6 months?
why: Black Sea war risk and Balkan droughts dominate the world sunflower oil supply.

title: Will sunflower oil be above $1600/mt in 3 months?
why: EU food processors depend on Ukrainian and Romanian sunflower oil.

title: Will rice be above $500/mt in 6 months?
why: Po valley droughts cut Italian rice, Europe's largest, while Asian export bans set world prices.

title: Will Italy declare a national drought emergency in 2027?
why: The 2022 Po drought led to regional emergencies; a national one would signal structural water stress.

title: Will an EU state restrict farmland purchases by non-EU sovereign funds by 2028?
why: Rules on foreign sovereign buyers decide who controls European food land as heat raises its value.

title: Will a Saudi or UAE state-linked fund announce a purchase of more than 10,000 ha of farmland in Southern or Eastern Europe by end of 2027?
why: Gulf states are securing food abroad; a large European purchase would tighten local supply and land prices.

title: Will Spain's 2027/28 olive oil output fall below 1.0 million tonnes?
why: Spain makes about 45% of the world's olive oil; two heat-hit seasons halved it to about 0.66 Mt.

title: Will Athens or a major Greek island impose household water rationing in 2027?
why: Athens reservoirs hit record lows in 2024-25; rationing would put farms and tourism in direct competition.

title: Will the post-2027 EU CAP ring-fence at least EUR 10 bn for farm heat and drought adaptation?
why: Whether Brussels funds adaptation at scale decides how fast southern farms can irrigate and switch crops.

title: Will Russia or Ukraine impose a grain export ban or Black Sea shipping halt lasting over 30 days by end of 2027?
why: The Black Sea ships about a quarter of world wheat; a halt would spike EU and North African bread prices.

title: Will France's 2027 soft wheat harvest come in below 30 million tonnes?
why: France is the EU's grain anchor; the wet-then-hot 2024 season cut it to about 26 Mt.
